source.text:
Hard disagree there. I work in video games and AI can one shot bugs that would have taken a normal programmer days unless they were already extremely familiar with the area - like you can literally go "the game crashes on the switch when the player does action X, here's a core dump, go" and it will either straight up find the issue immediately or it will get you 98% there. I've worked in games for a long time now and I love being thrown at all kinds of weird and unsolvable crashes and then spending hours looking over logs and GPU dumps, but I would be absolutely stupid to pretend like AI can't do this faster than I can.

For implementing brand new features - we can have a discussion here, there's definitely issues with even the best agents at doing large scale big engine changes. But bug solving and adding small-ish things in an existing code base it will do much faster than a human would, purely because it can find the right place and understand the layout of the code almost instantly.
